subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk require explicit realtime readiness before microphone/WebRTC startup, or should any resolved OpenAI Realtime-capable credential keep enabling Talk implicitly?
rationale: Current main intentionally accepts API-key or OAuth/Codex auth for Realtime, while this report expects a local/non-Realtime Talk setup not to enter OpenAI WebRTC; either answer changes user-facing setup semantics and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Gate on Gateway readiness preflight
options.body: Use talk.catalog or a dedicated Gateway readiness result to disable or block Talk before microphone startup unless the selected realtime provider is ready, and show a clear setup message.

options.title: Keep implicit credential activation
options.body: Treat API-key or OAuth/Codex OpenAI auth as enough to enable browser Talk, and narrow the remaining work to clearer provider/API error text when OpenAI rejects setup.

options.title: Require explicit realtime config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when talk.realtime is explicitly configured, accepting the upgrade impact for users who currently rely on auto-selected provider credentials.

recommendation.title: Gate on Gateway readiness preflight
recommendation.body: Use talk.catalog or a dedicated Gateway readiness result to disable or block Talk before microphone startup unless the selected realtime provider is ready, and show a clear setup message.

likelyOwner.reason: The newest merged auth-provider policy and docs for OpenAI Realtime voice came from this owner trail, so they are the best routing candidate for the activation contract choice.
